chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: 1950s: Minneapolis base and the Billy Williams Revue in Las Vegas
summary: From his Minneapolis Key Club band, Horace joined Billy Williams for the Riviera and Starlight Room in Vegas, six engagements, one of the first revues there, featuring trumpeter Clora Bryant and the Four Dukes.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. Then you got back to Chicago in late '49, 1950, according to my reports. One thing -- I basically just have information during the 1950's that you had your own group, small group, mainly in Minneapolis and Vegas, and various places.

Minneapolis was the base -- the jumping off place, I should say, with Billy Williams. Billy Williams brought his Charioteers to this particular Key Club where my band was housed, and he loved this group that I had so much so that he said to me one day, "Hey man, I've got a date in Vegas at the Riviera Theatre." He said, "Would you like to go?" I said, "Oh yes, sure." He said, "Well, it's comin' up in about three months," He says, "I'm gonna play a couple of shows down in Kansas City, and I'll get back to you." Well, I heard these things so much before --

-- I took it with a grain of salt. But one morning, at five o'clock the phone rang, and he says, "Hey man, this is Billy Williams. You ready to go to Vegas? We open up in two weeks." And man, this was three months afterwards. So I had to go talk to the boss which was Hank [Sabis.] He brought attractions in his club like Sarah Vaughn,

Slappy White, Billy Eckstein, the all these guys played there, you know, and my band backed these guys, you know? Redd Foxx was there. Redd Foxx came there and broke it up, man, just like he is doing, you know. So I had to get a leave of absence from the owner. I wanted an eight-week absence -- leave of absence to go play with Billy Williams. I'm still on that eight week absence. I never went back. But we went to Vegas and played the Riviera and the Starlight Room, six different times. First time, we went there for four weeks, and we stayed six months. That's a career.
Had a great band. We had a revue, and this is -- we were one of the first revues that ever played in --

-- Vegas. Then comes the George Young Revue, Harry James and Betty Grable in their revue. They all started there, you know what I mean. Revues I'm speaking of. But we broke it up. I had a quartet with me called the Four Dukes, and had a fat boy weighed 350 pounds that sang Mack the Knife. Tore it up. So we went on from there, and I had a good trumpet player named Clora Bryant who sang and played like Louis Armstrong. A woman.
She made some records with Billy Williams, man, she could play. We had an arrangement called Angel Eyes.
And she could hit high F's all night long, and she wasn't like the average woman, you know, (inaudible) As the night progressed, she got stronger. This could go on.
